To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the infectivity of commercial mycorrhiza products was affected by the substrate, 2) the inoculation of plants with mycorrhiza did not improve plant growth, and 3) the inoculation with some products increased the mycorrhizae colonization in the substrate.
the infectivity of commercial mycorrhiza inoculants was highly dependent on the growing medium, with some products performing better in one medium than in the other.

1) mycorrhizae can be successfully introduced to nursery crops by the use of mycorrhiza-inoculated seeds and mycorrhizala-inoculated soilless media; 2) the use of mycorriza-inoculated soil less media is a more efficient method than the use of myccorrhiza-inoculated seed; and 3) mycorrhiza inoculation does not increase plant growth.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of mycorrhiza infectivity of commercial inoculants under nursery conditions.
the assessment of the infectivity of ten mycorrhizae inoculants in nursery conditions.
the development of a method for evaluating the infectivity of commercial mycorrhiza inoculants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the infectivity of the commercial mycorrhiza inoculants tested was not as high as expected.
the commercial mycorrhiza products tested in this study were not able to promote plant growth in the conditions tested.
the commercial mycorrhiza inoculants are effective in promoting mycorrhizae in nursery conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mycorrhizae are not a panacea for all nursery problems, but they can be an important component in a well-balanced program of nursery management.

the commercial products are a valuable source of inoculum and that the use of these products in the nursery industry is a good strategy for the introduction of ectomycorrhizal fungi in forest plantations.
the infectivity of commercial mycorrhiza inoculants is influenced by growing medium and that mycorrhizae did not enhance plant performance in the conditions of our study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mycorrhizae can be used to increase plant growth and nutrient uptake in nursery conditions.
commercial mycorrhiza inoculants are not all equal in their ability to promote mycorrhizae.
mycorrhizas can be successfully established with commercial products, although there is variability in the infectivity of the different products.
